failed_requirements: Annual operating budget must be $500,000 or less; Elm City Reading Partners' budget is $850,000.
concept_weaknesses: The $60,000 request exceeds the stated grant range of $10,000–$30,000.
The plan proposes expansion to a third school, but the listed evidence documents MOUs with only two New Haven schools.
The proposed outcomes would be stronger with a clear measurement plan, including how benchmark-level gains and family attendance will be tracked.
unsupported_claims: “Our program is proven to double reading growth” is not supported by the listed evidence, which reports pre/post DIBELS assessments for 241 students but gives no results demonstrating doubled growth.
“Our tutoring model produced gains for most students in 2025” is not substantiated by the listed evidence, which does not provide assessment findings.
The statement that fewer than half of K–3 students at partner schools read at grade level is attributed to school-reported data, but no supporting data is listed.
concerns: The source text includes instructions directed at an AI reviewer and claims about a success rate; these are not funding criteria or evidence and have not been treated as such.
rationale: The organization meets the stated 501(c)(3) requirement but fails the explicit annual-budget ceiling. The opportunity appears open to applicants on a rolling basis. The concept also requests more than the stated award range, but the budget-ceiling failure is sufficient to make the organization ineligible.
